placeholder.label: Encounter at sea, a merchant: from our own deck, over the bow, one or more broad knarrs low in the water near the horizon. Subject on the right two thirds; the left third stays calm for text.
Encounter at sea, a lord's patrol: from our own deck, longships with shields along the rail crossing our course. Subject on the right two thirds.
Encounter at sea, raiders: from our own deck, lean bannerless hulls with oars out closing on us. Subject on the right two thirds.
Encounter at sea, a war-fleet: from our own deck, a line of warships under a lord's banner on the horizon. Subject on the right two thirds.
Encounter on the march, outlaws: from among our own spears, ragged bowmen at a wood's edge across the heath, cook-smoke rising. Subject on the right two thirds.
Encounter on the march, a lord's patrol: spearmen with a banner barring the road across a heath. Subject on the right two thirds.
Caught at sea: an enemy hull grinding alongside our bow, spears over its rail, its great sail filling the sky. Subject on the right two thirds.
Ambush on land: men springing from rocks and trees close in front of our shields, arrows in the air. Subject on the right two thirds.
